sections.heading: C — Speed, stopping, school buses
sections.markdown:
## C — Speed, stopping, school buses

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: FXsec06F01
Sit upright without tensing; position your hands at eight and four on an imagined clock face. Grip the steering wheel with fingers and thumbs rather than your palms [FXsec06F01].
Source: [FXsec06F01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: FXsec06F02
Taking the wheel makes you responsible for your actions; follow Virginia traffic rules and protect yourself, passengers and others using the road [FXsec06F02].
Source: [FXsec06F02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: FXsec06F03
A speed limit sets the highest lawful road speed when conditions are ideal [FXsec06F03].
Source: [FXsec06F03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: FXsec06F04
Reduce speed where signs show that a school-zone or work-zone speed restriction is active [FXsec06F04].
Source: [FXsec06F04 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: FXsec06F05
Follow posted speed restrictions. Slow further where school or work-zone signs apply, or where construction or poor weather makes that posted speed unsafe [FXsec06F05].
Source: [FXsec06F05 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: FXsec06F06
For passenger vehicles and motorcycles, default maxima are twenty-five miles per hour in school, business and residential areas, thirty-five on unpaved roads and fifty-five elsewhere, unless a speed sign sets another limit [FXsec06F06].
Source: [FXsec06F06 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: FXsec06F07
An active school or work-zone speed sign requires slower travel; construction or bad weather also requires slowing when the posted speed would be unsafe [FXsec06F07].
Source: [FXsec06F07 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: FXsec06F08
Travel below the speed limit is allowed provided it does not obstruct the normal movement of traffic [FXsec06F08].
Source: [FXsec06F08 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: FXsec06F09
The manual divides stopping distance into three factors: perception time, reaction distance and braking distance [FXsec06F09].
Source: [FXsec06F09 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: FXsec06F10
Wet pavement can make braking distance twice as long [FXsec06F10].
Source: [FXsec06F10 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: FXsec06F11
Bring the vehicle to a stop at every stop sign, red traffic light and flashing red signal [FXsec06F11].
Source: [FXsec06F11 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A02
Never pass a school bus while it loads or unloads: flashing red signals and the extended stop sign both command a full stop [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: FXsec06F13
A stopped bus with flashing red lights and its stop arm out requires stopping from either direction until everyone is clear and the bus moves. Loading or unloading also requires a stop if its signals are off. Opposing traffic need not stop when a median or barrier separates it from the bus, but must watch for unexpected movements by people leaving it [FXsec06F13].
Source: [FXsec06F13 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: FXsec06F14
Unless signs set a different limit, passenger vehicles and motorcycles may travel no faster than twenty-five miles per hour in school, business and residential areas [FXsec06F14].
Source: [FXsec06F14 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
